item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q023_homeodomain_heterogeneous_fold","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1p7jd_ (SUNID 94286) and d1ztra1 (SUNID 125655) share the Homeodomain family a.4.1.1 (SUNID 46690), not merely the Homeodomain-like superfamily a.4.1, DNA/RNA-binding 3-helical-bundle fold a.4, or all-alpha class. Common ancestry/homology therefore remains justified; the domain-scoped, non-inherited hf flag on d1ztra1 does not cancel the family relationship. It instead records structural heterogeneity: d1ztra1 adopts a fold different from the family exemplar despite similar sequence and secondary-structure count. Consequently, family membership or sequence similarity alone cannot justify assuming that d1ztra1 and d1p7jd_ have interchangeable topology, residue correspondences, packing, or structural superpositions. Template use requires direct structural/topological validation, and identical ligand/DNA specificity or function should not be transferred solely from the family assignment. They also should not be treated as independent examples of one homogeneous fold in training: d1ztra1 must retain its hf caveat to avoid contradictory structural labels, sequence-related leakage, and biased evaluation. Experimental context matters as well: both are annotated mutants, while d1p7jd_ is additionally annotated as complexed with NHE.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__compare_scop_domains","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1p7jd_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1p7jd_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1p7jd_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1p7jd_/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ztra1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ztra1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ztra1/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ztra1/homology"]}]}
